channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, China Coordinate Logistics Along Middle Corridor
item.description: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and China are strengthening the Middle Corridor as a trans-Eurasian trade route. China's proposal to extend its logistics chain to Baku, coupled with expanded capacity at Aktau and new transport agreements, integrates existing infrastructure. This aims to enhance freight connectivity with Europe and offer alternative routes for Japan and South Korea, though long-term viability depends on coordinated services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Secures $3 Billion IFC Infrastructure Investment Amid Arbitration Loss
item.description: Kazakhstan received a $3 billion commitment from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) for infrastructure projects, focusing on public-private partnerships and water resource management. However, this positive development was overshadowed by a Hague arbitration court's decision to dismiss $12 billion in Kazakh claims against Western oil giants concerning the Kashagan oil field dispute.

item.title: Uzbekistan's agricultural reforms gain international recognition from FAO Director-General
item.description: The effectiveness of Uzbekistan's agricultural reforms is being recognized internationally, according to the Ministry of Agriculture. FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu praised the country's progress during a meeting in the US, noting reforms serve as an example for other nations. He highlighted the importance of agriculture in food security, resource management, and global food system resilience.

item.title: Almaty police fine woman for spreading false information about 102 emergency response
item.description: Almaty police have fined a woman for disseminating false information after she posted a video on Instagram alleging delayed response to a 102 call. Police investigation revealed officers arrived promptly, but the caller did not open the door or answer calls. The woman was penalized for spreading misinformation.

item.title: UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh enters race for UN Secretary-General
item.description: Veteran UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh has announced her candidacy for the position of United Nations Secretary-General, aiming to succeed António Guterres. Nusseibeh, who played a key role on Afghanistan during the UAE's UN Security Council term, pledges to push the UN to act earlier in crises and deliver concrete results, rebuilding trust and ensuring meaningful change.

item.title: NVIDIA reveals plans to expand AI infrastructure in Kazakhstan
item.description: NVIDIA has announced plans to expand Kazakhstan's AI infrastructure in collaboration with Kazakhtelecom and Firebird AI. This includes deploying GPUs, supporting local startups, and developing AI applications. The announcement coincided with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's visit to Astana, where he met with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and discussed the country's potential as a global AI power provider.

item.title: Over 10,000 Kazakhs Over 50 Employed Through Government Program
item.description: More than 10,000 Kazakh citizens over the age of 50 have found employment through the 'Silver Age' state program in the first nine months of the year. Agriculture was the most popular sector, followed by services and education. The program subsidizes wages for participants.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Discuss Joint Nuclear Power Plant Ventures
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia held a conference in Tashkent to discuss establishing joint ventures for building a nuclear power plant in Uzbekistan. Representatives from Uzatom, Rosatom, and leading Uzbek and Russian companies participated. The focus was on expanding domestic enterprise involvement and developing industrial cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Thailand Discuss Direct Flights and Middle Corridor Development
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ambassador to Thailand, Margulan Baimukhan, met with Urassa Mongkolnavin to discuss cooperation. Key areas include transport, logistics, the Middle Corridor, digitalization, tourism, and direct air travel. They also explored collaboration in education, healthcare, and culture.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture to Receive First Satellite Images Soon
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture will soon receive and begin processing the first images from its national satellite by the end of October. These images will be shared with farmers via the iDiykan app, which is currently in its final testing phase and will be synchronized with land registry and animal tracking systems.

item.title: Tajikistan Social Security Agency Responds to ADB Pension Age Proposal
item.description: Responding to the Asian Development Bank's (ADB) recommendation to raise the retirement age in Tajikistan, the Social Security and Pension Agency stated the proposal is advisory and does not alter current legislation. The ADB suggested gradually increasing the women's retirement age from 58 to 63 or to 65 for both genders.

item.title: Russia confirms proposal for Russia-US-China talks on Ukraine conflict
item.description: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko stated that while a final agreement for Russia-US-China talks on Ukraine has not been reached, all three parties show interest. The Kremlin confirmed the possibility of dialogue is being considered, with Russia proposing the meeting during the APEC summit in China.

item.title: Case reopened against son of Aris mayor in traffic accident that injured student
item.description: A criminal case has been reopened concerning a traffic accident on the Astana-Pavlodar highway where a 21-year-old student lost both legs. The driver was identified as the son of the Aris mayor. The victim's sister confirmed the case's reopening and stated the family continues to demand a full investigation.

item.title: Residents of homes near Atyrau oil refinery may be relocated
item.description: The boundaries of the sanitary protection zone of the Atyrau oil refinery have been defined, potentially leading to the relocation of nearby homes. A working commission has been established to advise residents on resettlement, property valuation, and compensation. Meetings with residents are planned for mid-November.

item.title: Kurultai to Consider Amendments to Eurasian Economic Union Treaty
item.description: The Kurultai will review proposed amendments to the Eurasian Economic Union Treaty. These changes will affect the internal market, technical regulation, trade in services, investment, competition, public procurement, and the common electricity market. A commission will also consider a loan agreement between Kazakhstan and the Asian Development Bank.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Cooperation with OSCE Parliamentary Assembly
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber Speaker met with the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly delegation led by its President. Discussions focused on enhancing cooperation, human rights protection, decent labor conditions, and labor migration regulation. Uzbekistan highlighted its reforms and engagement with international parliamentary bodies. The OSCE praised Uzbekistan's regional initiatives.

item.title: Atyrau Refinery Sanitary Zone: Resettlement Commission Formed for Residents
item.description: Atyrau Refinery has clarified the boundaries of its sanitary protection zone, necessitating the resettlement of residents. An interdepartmental commission has been established to manage the relocation process. A final registry of affected properties will be published after cadastral verification. Compensation payments and independent property valuations will be addressed.

item.title: Kazakh President Emphasizes Sovereignty and Independence as Priceless Treasures
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that sovereignty and independence are the nation's most valuable treasures during a ceremony for Republic Day. He praised the older generation for their hard work and overcoming challenges, and noted the positive trend of youth respecting national history. He stressed strengthening statehood as a sacred duty.

item.title: NVIDIA CEO Proposes Kazakhstan as Global Physical AI Hub
item.description: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang met with President Tokayev in Astana, proposing Kazakhstan as a hub for global Physical AI. Huang highlighted Kazakhstan's potential in energy and skilled personnel for AI development. He noted the need for energy resources and knowledgeable individuals in science, math, and technology for AI advancement.

item.title: NVIDIA Acknowledges Kazakhtelecom's Role in Developing Kazakhstan's AI Infrastructure
item.description: Tech giant NVIDIA has announced its collaboration with Kazakhtelecom and Firebird AI to expand computing infrastructure in Kazakhstan. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang visited Astana, meeting with students and tech startups. The company highlighted its partnership with Kazakhtelecom and Firebird AI in developing computing power based on NVIDIA technologies.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens Pilot Plant for Lithium-Ion Battery Recycling
item.description: Kazakhstan's al-Farabi National University has launched a pilot plant to recycle used lithium-ion batteries. The facility will test technologies for processing and extracting valuable metals and materials. The process involves safely discharging, shredding, and sorting batteries to obtain a 'black mass' containing active materials for further component extraction. This initiative aims to integrate scientific developments into production and address environmental concerns.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Average Salary Exceeds 486,000 Tenge in Q2 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan's average monthly salary reached 486,388 tenge in the second quarter of 2026, according to the Bureau of National Statistics. While this represents an 8.4% annual increase, the real wage index, adjusted for inflation, decreased by 1.8%. The median salary was 348,415 tenge, with 58.4% of workers earning over 300,000 tenge.

item.title: Khalilzad Warns of Worsening Afghanistan-Pakistan Relations Amid Recruitment Allegations
item.description: Former U.S. special representative Zalmay Khalilzad has warned that relations between Afghanistan and Pakistan could significantly deteriorate. He cited numerous reports alleging Pakistani recruitment and arming of Afghans to fight insurgents and the Taliban. Khalilzad cautioned that current tensions make further worsening of ties between Kabul and Islamabad likely.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Addresses 'Doolot Kurulush' Shareholder Issues
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov addressed concerns of approximately 3,000 shareholders of the 'Doolot Kurulush' company, who were allegedly defrauded. The state has intervened, finding investors and arranging settlements, with one square meter costing around $920. A Chinese investor has injected $25 million to resume construction, with the project expected to be completed within three years to recoup investment.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Increase Oil Supplies via Azerbaijan to 1.7 Million Tons
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to increase oil supplies via Azerbaijan by over 40% next year, reaching 1.7 million tons. KazMunayGas is negotiating increased volumes for the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline. The route's viability depends on economic conditions and tariffs, but it will not replace the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC).

item.title: Kazakh President Awards NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with Dostyk Order of Merit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev awarded NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang the Order of Merit, First Class, during a meeting in Akorda. Tokayev highlighted the significance of Huang's visit in strengthening bilateral cooperation and developing Kazakhstan's artificial intelligence ecosystem. Huang praised Kazakhstan's strategy to become an AI country and proposed it as a global hub for Physical AI.

item.title: 628 Gas Stations in Uzbekistan Fail to Meet Safe Distance Requirements from Residential Areas
item.description: A total of 628 gas stations in Uzbekistan have been identified as not meeting the minimum 125-meter safe distance requirement from residential areas. While a draft law on industrial safety is being improved, deputies removed a specific sanction for violating this norm, considering corruption risks and potential shutdowns.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Offers Condolences to China Over Deadly Tibet Earthquake
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov has sent a telegram of condolences to Chinese President Xi Jinping following a powerful earthquake in the Tibet Autonomous Region that resulted in fatalities and injuries. Japarov expressed deep sympathy on behalf of the Kyrgyz people to the families of the victims and wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

item.title: Trump Claims Musk Lifted Starlink Restrictions in Ukraine, Kyiv Reports Ongoing Issues
item.description: Amidst growing disputes over restrictions on Ukraine's vital "Starlink" satellite internet service, U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that the company's head, Elon Musk, had lifted limitations on Kyiv's use of the service. Trump stated, "He brought them back to where they were." This statement followed President Zelensky's confirmation to CNN of ongoing difficulties.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang visits Astana, discusses AI and energy
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met with Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in Astana. Huang announced Nvidia's investment in AI company Higgsfield and praised Kazakhstan's ambition to become an AI nation. He suggested exporting intelligence by leveraging the country's energy resources for AI computing infrastructure, like data centers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to restore 100,000 hectares of pastures
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to restore 100,000 hectares of pastures, President Sadyr Japarov announced. Responding to a livestock farmer's concerns about pasture scarcity, Japarov stated that restoration efforts began in 2021. He aims to return degraded areas to their former state, a process estimated to take 15-20 years with regular reseeding. Farmers can access preferential loans for support.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev awards Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with Dostyk Order
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev awarded Nvidia co-founder and president Jensen Huang the Dostyk Order of the First Degree for his contributions to AI development in Kazakhstan. During their meeting, Huang proposed making Kazakhstan a global hub for Physical AI, citing the country's energy resources and skilled specialists. Tokayev praised Nvidia's partnership with Higgsfield.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Explains Impact of National Fund Transfers on Inflation
item.description: The Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Bank, Timur Suleimenov, explained how additional transfers from the National Fund will affect inflation. In 2027, 4.43 trillion tenge are planned for the budget from the fund. Suleimenov noted that significant money influxes have an inflationary effect, prompting the National Bank to adjust its monetary policy corridor.

item.title: Woman Reports Kyrgyz Citizen Defrauding Compatriots in Russia to President
item.description: A resident of Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov regarding a Kyrgyz citizen allegedly defrauding around 50-60 compatriots working in Russia. The total alleged damages exceed $100 million, with the woman claiming the suspect owes her $15 million. The president has instructed the Interior Ministry to investigate.

item.title: Kazatomprom to Reconsider Uranium Sale Deal with Russian Company
item.description: Kazakhstan's national atomic company, Kazatomprom, will again put to shareholders a deal to sell natural uranium to Russia's Uranium One Group, a subsidiary of Rosatom. Shareholders previously rejected the transaction. Technical changes have been made to the contract, but key commercial terms remain the same. The previous vote saw a majority of shareholders abstain.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases for Fifth Consecutive Day
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has fallen for the fifth consecutive day. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 24. This marks a continued trend of depreciation for the US dollar.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Suggested to Hold People's Kurultai Every Four Years
item.description: During a meeting with residents, a citizen proposed to Sadyr Japarov that the People's Kurultai be held every four years instead of annually, citing costs. President Japarov acknowledged the suggestion, stating that the frequency could be adjusted in the future.

item.title: Turkmen Citizen Dies in Severe Flooding in Istanbul
item.description: A Turkmen citizen has died in severe floods that hit Istanbul following heavy rainfall. The body of the 30-year-old, identified as Myrat Babajanov, was found in the Golden Horn. This brings the total death toll from the floods to five, with two others still missing. The floods caused significant damage to numerous buildings and vehicles.

item.title: American Investor Plans to Expand Vegetable Processing Plant in Kashkadarya
item.description: Wosune International plans to increase its investment in fruit and vegetable processing in Uzbekistan's Kashkadarya region to $50 million. The company, which has already invested $8.5 million, aims to produce high-quality dehydrated products for international markets, including major companies like Nestlé and Mars. The expanded facility will create 150 jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Only 18% Pass State Language Exam on First Attempt
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, only 18% of participants are passing the state language exam on their first try. Even potential presidential candidates Omurbek Suvanaliyev and Siymik Japiqayev failed to score enough points on the Kyrgyz language test. Japiqayev retook the test.
